grammar_focus: Present simple vs present continuous; state verbs
grammar_html:
• zvyky, opakované děje
I usually get up at six.
děj probíhající právě teď
Shh, the baby is sleeping.

• fakta, obecné pravdy
Water boils at 100 °C.
dočasná situace „v těchto dnech“
I'm working from home this week.

• trvalé stavy
She lives in Brno.
měnící se a vyvíjející se situace
Prices are going up.

• signální slova: always, usually, often, every day, never
signální slova: now, at the moment, today, this week, currently, Look! Listen!

Stavová slovesa (state verbs) se v průběhovém čase obvykle nepoužívají: know, understand, believe, think (= mít názor), like, love, hate, prefer, want, need, mean, seem, belong, own, remember.
✗ I'm knowing him. → ✓ I know him.

Slovesa se dvěma významy: I think it's a good idea (názor) × I'm thinking about my holiday (přemýšlím); She has two cats (vlastní) × She's having lunch (jí); He is rude (povaha) × He's being rude (právě teď se tak chová).

always + průběhový čas = něco nás opakovaně rozčiluje: He's always leaving his socks on the floor!

exercises.q: She always does what she promises. → (bossy / reliable / stubborn / thoughtful)
He never gives money to anyone. → (absent-minded / mean / reliable / talkative)
She tells everyone what to do. → (bossy / cheerful / reliable / talkative)
He changes his mind about nothing – ever. → (absent-minded / cheerful / stubborn / talkative)
She's happy and smiling most of the time. → (cheerful / mean / stubborn / thoughtful)
He talks a lot, even to strangers on the bus. → (bossy / mean / talkative / thoughtful)
She always remembers your birthday and asks how you are. → (absent-minded / cheerful / reliable / thoughtful)
He forgets where he put his phone every day. → (absent-minded / bossy / mean / stubborn)
I (work / 'm working) from home this week because they're repairing our office.

Look! It (snows / 's snowing)!

This soup (tastes / is tasting) delicious.
He's usually very polite, but today he (is / is being) really rude.
